findings.title: Native replay guard bypassed by --kicad-cli alone
findings.message: The guard that stops native checks from being re-enabled implicitly is skipped when only --kicad-cli is passed. The error text says --require-erc must be passed explicitly, but the check does not enforce it. A replay with just a tool path then sets KiCadCLI without RequireERC, so native-check behavior is ambiguous and the replay may differ from the recorded run.
findings.suggestion: Require --require-erc whenever the original run requested native KiCad, regardless of whether --kicad-cli is set. Also make the error message match what is actually enforced.

findings.title: Off-by-one file limit and all-or-nothing publish on oversize output
findings.message: The docs and capability inventory advertise a 256-file maximum, but Publish rejects 256 files (>= check). It also fails the whole bundle without writing it, so all evidence is lost if any single file or the total exceeds the limits. For example, a large ngspice stdout over 2 MiB in ngspice-command.json would discard the entire failure bundle. The limit check is also inconsistent with Verify.
findings.suggestion: Align the limit semantics with the documentation, counting manifest.json explicitly. Truncate oversized captured stdout/stderr before putting it in the bundle, so a failing run still saves evidence.
